$comment: nen's own self-declaration: what `nen shu` runs when it is pointed at THIS repository. No `dependency` block -- nen does not pin itself to a released version of itself, and there is no bootstrap to re-fetch from inside the checkout that builds it. `stack` has no member for a Bun-native CLI among the seven this release's reference pack documents (compose-desktop, dotnet-winui, expo, gatsby, gradle-android, nextjs, xcode-ios); the field is a free string everywhere it is read (src/schema/contract.ts's `parseLanes` calls `requireString`, not `requireEnum`), so `bun-cli` is written as the honest name for this stack rather than borrowed from one of the seven.

release-guard.$comment: The focused lane for src/dev/release-publish.ts, the publisher behind `verbs.nen.release`. Its fixtures are hermetic and offline: a throwaway git repository with tags and a changelog, `gh` faked, proving notes composition, the multi-version gap, the DERIVED tag, --latest withheld for an older tag, the github.com-only host refusal, repository access certified before a ref 404 is read, a failed create classified as gh's defect, and every refusal -- publishing nothing, ever.

nen.why: The dependency install has been run (`bun install`). Nen asserts this and never performs it -- an install runs this project's own scripts.

build.why: There is no compile step for a `bun run` binary; `tsc --noEmit` is the closest fact this repository has to a build -- the same check `bun run typecheck` runs in CI.

test.why: Aka owns this full regression. Collect instrumented LCOV counts and JUnit results in the same run; touched-file measurement/gating is deferred to mukai. Focused authoring/checkpoint tests use the explicit scoped lane without coverage.

argv: const file = Bun.file('coverage/lcov.info'); if (!(await file.exists()) || file.size === 0) throw new Error('Missing or empty aka coverage capture');
coverage.why: Mukai only verifies the aka-captured LCOV artifact is nonempty, then Nen parses it. This row runs no tests and deletes no result. Hatsu verifies source-tree/configuration provenance before calling it; a stale or missing capture returns to aka regression.

dev.why: There is no server to run in dev mode -- `nen` is a one-shot CLI. `--help` is the fastest real invocation that exercises the entry point without needing a target repository or GitHub credentials.

archive.why: The one compiled binary this machine's host can produce (`bun build --compile --target=bun-darwin-arm64`); `linux-x64` and `windows-x64` are the other two release targets and are left to CI, which builds all three.

ui-test.unsupported: nen is a CLI with no UI surface; there is no browser or simulator suite to run.

run.unsupported: nen has no production/staging serve mode distinct from `dev` -- it is a one-shot binary invocation, not a long-running server.

release.why: Publishes ONE GitHub Release for the newest v* tag (named as DERIVED) that already resolves on origin, notes from that tag's own CHANGELOG.md section; refuses before anything is sent if origin is not on github.com, the repository is not readable, or the tag is absent, missing on the remote, or already released. Cuts no tag, pushes nothing, uploads no asset -- release-assets attaches the binaries on `release: published`. G3 (CON-6) holds the go; this row is what mugetsu RUNS, never permission to run it.
release.$comment: RETIRED SEAT, 2026-09-22, following zheref/hatsu's identical fix of 2026-09-19. This row previously read: "publishing is `nen tag cut` plus a GitHub Release the maintainer creates by hand; there is no single local publish step nen can declare for itself." -- false in practice: v0.12.0, v0.13.0, v0.13.1 and v0.14.0 were each published by an agent session running `gh release create` on the maintainer's credentials after the maintainer's G3 go, and the seat made `hatsu:mugetsu` (which runs `nen shu release`) stop at exit 4, so publication happened outside the declared machinery. A declaration that disagrees with the practice is a bug in the declaration. The publisher is TypeScript in src/dev/ rather than Hatsu's bash because bootstrap/nen.sh is the one shell file this repository ships (AK-11) and D16 bars a runtime python3. --tag is omitted deliberately: `nen shu release` passes no arguments, so the script derives the newest v* tag.

deploy.unsupported: nen ships as release binaries fetched by `bootstrap/nen.sh`, not as a deploy to a named destination.

test.why: The focused authored lane for reusable device-record extraction: pure resolution, schema, launch integration and the executor's toolchain-independence guard.

The publisher's hermetic --self-test. Run it as `nen shu test --lane release-guard --repo <nen>` when src/dev/release-publish.ts changes; src/dev/release-publish.test.ts carries the same fixtures into the vitest regression.
